sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Inventory vs. Sales / COGS Trend: Inventory intensity changed +36.3 percentage points of total assets and inventory days moved +105 days. Stock is building faster than sales, a classic early warning of demand weakness or channel stuffing.
CFO vs. Net Income Conversion: Operating cash flow converted 68% of reported net profit. Profit is running ahead of cash generation, which points to working-capital or accrual quality issues.
FCF Generation Consistency: Free cash flow was positive in 3 of the last 5 reported years. Repeated FCF deficits mean growth is being funded by the balance sheet rather than by the business.
Current Ratio Liquidity: Current assets cover current liabilities 0.85 times. Liquidity is tight relative to short-term obligations.
Share Dilution Check: The share count changed +41.8% a year. Dilution transfers value from existing holders to new issuance.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 65 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded -7.2% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 4 hard red flags and 3 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 74/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
